# tina4-nodejs — LLM Context

Tina4 Node.js/TypeScript v3.13.88. 98 built-in features, zero dependencies. Web framework for Node.js 20+.
Routes, ORM, templates, auth, queue, websocket, graphql, WSDL — all built in. ESM only.

Install: npm install tina4-nodejs
Version: 3.10.70
Default port: 7148 (config priority: explicit > PORT env var > 7148)

---

## Router (File-Based)

Route files go in src/routes/. Filename = HTTP method. Directory path = URL path.

```
src/routes/
  api/
    users/
      get.ts          → GET /api/users
      post.ts         → POST /api/users
      [id]/
        get.ts        → GET /api/users/{id}
        put.ts        → PUT /api/users/{id}
        delete.ts     → DELETE /api/users/{id}
```

Each route file exports a default async function:

```typescript
import type { Tina4Request, Tina4Response } from "@tina4/core";

export default async function (req: Tina4Request, res: Tina4Response) {
  return res.json({ users: [] });
}

// Optional Swagger metadata
export const meta = { summary: "List all users", tags: ["Users"] };

// Optional template rendering
export const template = "page.twig";
```

### Explicit Route Registration

```typescript
import { Router } from "@tina4/core";

Router.get("/api/users", async (req, res) => {
  return res.json({ users: [] });
});

Router.post("/api/users", async (req, res) => {
  const body = req.body;
  return res.json({ created: body.name }, 201);
});

Router.get("/api/users/{id}", async (req, res) => {
  const id = req.params.id;
  return res.json({ id });
});

// Auth control via JSDoc comments
/** @noauth */
Router.post("/api/public", async (req, res) => {
  return res.json({ open: true });
});

/** @secure */
Router.get("/api/private", async (req, res) => {
  return res.json({ secret: true });
});
```

---

## Database

```typescript
import { initDatabase } from "@tina4/orm";

const db = await initDatabase("sqlite:///app.db"); // or postgres://, mysql://, mssql://, firebird://

const result = await db.fetch("SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ?", [true], 10, 0);
const row = await db.fetchOne("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", [1]);
await db.execute("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)", ["Alice"]);
await db.insert("users", { name: "Alice" });
await db.update("users", { id: 1, name: "Bob" });
await db.delete("users", { id: 1 });
const nextId = await db.getNextId("users"); // race-safe atomic ID generation
```

---

## ORM (Convention-Based Models)

Models go in src/models/. Export a default class with static tableName and fields:

```typescript
export default class User {
  static tableName = "users";
  static fields = {
    id:    { type: "integer" as const, primaryKey: true, autoIncrement: true },
    name:  { type: "string" as const,  required: true },
    email: { type: "string" as const,  required: true },
    active: { type: "boolean" as const, default: true },
  };
}
```

Field types: "string", "text", "integer", "number", "boolean", "datetime"
Field options: primaryKey, autoIncrement, required, default, minLength, maxLength, min, max, pattern

Auto-CRUD is generated from models: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE at /api/{tableName}.
File-based routes override auto-CRUD when both match.

---

## Frond (Templates)

```typescript
// In a route file
export const template = "page.twig";

// Or programmatically
res.render("page.twig", { title: "Home", items });
```

Templates use Twig syntax. Located in src/templates/.

---

## Auth

```typescript
import { Auth } from "@tina4/core";

const token = Auth.getToken({ userId: 1, role: "admin" });
const payload = Auth.validToken(token); // returns object or null
const hashed = Auth.hashPassword("secret");
const valid = Auth.checkPassword("secret", hashed);
```

---

## Queue

```typescript
import { Queue } from "@tina4/core";

const queue = new Queue("emails", 3); // topic, maxRetries
await queue.push({ to: "alice@example.com", subject: "Hello" });

for await (const job of queue.consume("emails")) {
  process(job.payload);
  job.complete(); // or job.fail("reason")
}

await queue.produce("other_topic", { data: "value" });
const dead = await queue.deadLetters();
```

Backends: file (default), RabbitMQ, Kafka, MongoDB — configured via TINA4_QUEUE_BACKEND env var.

---

## Events

```typescript
import { Events } from "@tina4/core";

Events.on("user.created", (user) => {
  console.log(`Welcome ${(user as any).name}`);
});

Events.emit("user.created", { name: "Alice" });
Events.once("app.ready", () => console.log("Started!"));
```

---

## Project Structure

```
src/
  routes/       # File-based routes (auto-discovered)
  models/       # ORM model definitions (auto-registered)
  templates/    # Frond/Twig templates
  public/       # Static files served at /
migrations/     # SQL migration files
test/           # Test files
app.ts          # Entry point
package.json    # Dependencies
tsconfig.json   # TypeScript config
.env            # Environment variables
```

---

## Entry Point (app.ts)

```typescript
import { startServer } from "@tina4/core";

const port = parseInt(process.env.PORT || "7149", 10);
const host = process.env.HOST || "0.0.0.0";
startServer({ port, host });
```

---

## Known Gotchas

1. ESM only — use .js extensions in imports: `import { Router } from "./router.js"`
2. No Express/Fastify — uses native node:http
3. No decorators — convention-based models with static properties
4. Route dynamic params use {id} in URLs, [id] in directory names
5. POST/PUT/DELETE require auth by default. Use `/** @noauth */` JSDoc to make public
6. GET is public by default. Use `/** @secure */` JSDoc to protect
7. Queue job payload accessed via job.payload not job.data
8. All packages use barrel exports — import from "@tina4/core", "@tina4/orm", not internal paths
9. Default port: 7148 (NOT 7145)
10. TypeScript strict mode, ES2022 target, Node16 module resolution

## Scaffolding (`tina4nodejs generate`)
Scaffold boilerplate instead of hand-writing it: `tina4nodejs generate <feature>` for model, route, crud,
migration, service, queue, validator, seeder, websocket, listener, form, view, auth. Generated write
routes are secure by default (token-gated; pass `--public` to open them); reads are public. Logic
stubs carry an AI-FILL fill-spec placeholder (Intent/Given/Use/Return/Ground + a loud not-implemented
throw) — fill only that; working CRUD carries a lighter EXTEND marker.
